Paul calls himself a servant of Christ Jesus, set apart for the gospel. What has God set you apart for?
Paul longed to see the Roman believers so they could encourage each other. Who encourages your faith?
Paul says he is not ashamed of the gospel. Why is the gospel "the power of God for salvation"?
People exchanged the truth about God for a lie. What things are we tempted to worship in place of God?
Paul describes what happens when people turn from God. What does this show about our need for him?
God's kindness is meant to lead us to repentance. How has God's kindness drawn you back?
God shows no partiality. How does this shape how you see yourself and others?
Paul speaks of the law written on hearts. What does your conscience tell you about right and wrong?
True belonging to God is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit. What matters more to God than outward signs?
Even if people are unfaithful, God remains faithful. How does God's faithfulness comfort you?
"None is righteous, no, not one." Why is it important to see this clearly?
We are justified by God's grace as a gift through Christ. What does it mean that righteousness is a gift?
Paul says boasting is excluded. Why does grace leave no room for pride?
Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness. What does faith look like in your life?
The promise came to Abraham before he was circumcised. Why does Paul say it rests on faith, not law?
Abraham grew strong in faith, giving glory to God. What promise of God do you need to trust?
Jesus was delivered for our trespasses and raised for our justification. What do his death and resurrection mean for you?
We have peace with God and hope that does not put us to shame. How does suffering produce hope?
Christ died for us while we were still sinners. What does this show about God's love?
Through Adam came death, through Christ the free gift of life. How does Paul compare the two?
Where sin increased, grace abounded all the more. Where do you need to hear this today?
We were buried with Christ so that we might walk in newness of life. What does new life look like for you?
Paul says to consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God. How could that change how you face temptation?
Present your body to God as an instrument for righteousness. How can you offer yourself to God today?
The free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus. What does this gift mean to you?
We serve in the new way of the Spirit, not the old way of the written code. What is the difference?
Paul says the law is holy, righteous and good. Why then can't the law save us?
Paul says, "I do not do what I want." When have you felt this struggle?
Paul cries, "Who will deliver me?" and answers, "Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ." Where do you need this rescue?
"There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." What does this mean for you today?
The Spirit testifies that we are children of God. How does knowing you are God's child shape you?
Paul says present sufferings are not worth comparing with the coming glory. How does this hope help you now?
The Spirit helps us in our weakness when we do not know what to pray. What comfort is this?
Nothing can separate us from the love of God in Christ. Which item on Paul's list do you most need to hear?
Paul grieved deeply for his own people. Who do you long to see come to know God?
Paul says it depends not on human will but on God who has mercy. What does this teach you about mercy?
Paul pictures God as the potter. How do you respond to God's right to shape your life?
Some pursued righteousness by works and stumbled over Christ. Why do people stumble over grace?
Paul prays for those with zeal but without knowledge. What is the difference between zeal and true faith?
"Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." What does this promise mean for everyone?
"How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news!" How can you share the good news?
Faith comes from hearing the word of Christ. How is God's word building your faith?
God has kept a remnant chosen by grace. What does this show about God's faithfulness?
Paul warns the Gentiles not to be proud but to stand fast through faith. Where might pride creep into your faith?
"The gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable." What comfort does this give?
Paul bursts into praise at the depth of God's wisdom. What about God moves you to praise?
Paul urges you to be a living sacrifice and be transformed by renewing your mind. What area of your thinking needs renewing?
Each member has different gifts. What gifts has God given you for the church?
"Let love be genuine." Which phrase in these verses challenges you most?
"Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good." Who could you bless instead of resent?
Paul talks about respecting governing authorities. How can you be a good citizen as a follower of Jesus?
"Love is the fulfilling of the law." How does love sum up all the commands?
Paul says to wake up and put on the Lord Jesus Christ. What does that look like in your daily routine?
Paul says not to despise or judge those whose convictions differ. Where do you need to accept others?
Paul urges us to pursue what makes for peace and mutual upbuilding. How can you build someone up?
The kingdom of God is righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit. Which do you need most?
Paul says not to let food destroy the work of God. What freedoms might you give up for someone else's sake?
We who are strong should bear with the weak, as Christ did. Who can you help carry?
Scripture was written for our instruction and hope. How has the Bible given you hope?
Paul prays that the God of hope fills you with joy and peace in believing. Pray this for yourself and someone else.
Paul shared his plans and asked for prayer. What could you ask others to pray for?
Paul greets many people by name and thanks them for their work. Who could you thank for their faithfulness?
Paul says to be wise as to what is good and innocent as to what is evil. What does that look like for you?
"The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet." What hope does this give?
Paul passes on greetings from his co-workers and ends with grace. Who are the people you serve God alongside?
